title: Canonical cycle quotient comparison from derived lower truncation
statement: Let $C,D$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with chosen derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with enough injectives and K-injective resolutions in $C$. Let $F:C\to D$ be additive and left exact [def-sp-left-exact-additive], and $I$ a K-injective cochain complex [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. For $n\in\mathbf Z$, suppose $H^n(RF(QI))\to H^n(RF(\tau_{\ge n}QI))$ is an isomorphism, where $Q$ is localization and truncation is canonical [def-weil-t-structure]. Write $h$ for the left part of the chosen degree-n homology data: $h.i:h.K\to I^n$ is the kernel of $d^n$, $h.f\prime:I^{n-1}\to h.K$ is the induced boundary map, and $h.\pi:h.K\to h.H$ is its cokernel. Then the canonical map $\operatorname{coker}(F(h.f\prime))\to F(h.H)$ induced by $F(h.\pi)$ is an isomorphism. This is a statement about this actual cokernel-descending map, not the existence of an unrelated isomorphism.

proof.text: Put A=truncLE n I and B=truncGE n A. Kernel preservation identifies H^n(F(A)) with H^n(F(I)). The derived comparison for I is invertible because a quasi-isomorphism between K-injectives is a homotopy equivalence, preserved by additive F.

Left exactness gives the upper-truncation isomorphism on H^n after deriving. Naturality makes the derived comparison for A invertible. The assumed lower-truncation isomorphism, transported through upper truncation, identifies H^n(RF(QA)) with H^n(RF(QB)). Bottom derived cohomology of B is F(H^n(I)).

In the natural comparison square for A to B, the degree-n map is the projection from cycles to homology. Kernel uniqueness identifies the cycles of F(I) with F(h.K); their boundaries are the image of F(h.f\prime), so their quotient is the displayed cokernel. Its induced map is the composite isomorphism above: both have composite F(h.pi) with cokernel.pi, and cokernel uniqueness forces equality. Empty or zero objects and all integer degrees require no extra hypotheses.

mathlib_searches.query: A left exact additive functor on a K injective complex has canonical section cycle quotient isomorphism when the derived lower truncation projection induces a homology isomorphism
For a left exact additive functor and a K injective complex, canonical cokernel of mapped boundaries to mapped cycles computes mapped homology if derived lower truncation induces homology isomorphism
mathlib_searches.results: Generic homological functors, homologyFunctorFactors, and exact functors preserving homology. No left-exact K-injective canonical quotient comparison.

Generic truncation isomorphism and quasi-isomorphism declarations in Mathlib; no derived affine-evaluation theorem. The project AffineDerivedSectionsTruncationIso is a similar theorem for Spec with transported scalars, whose proof supplies the present route.

theorem kInjective_section_cycle_comparison
    {C : Type u} {D : Type u'} [Category.{v} C] [Category.{v'} D]
    [Abelian C] [Abelian D] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} C] [HasDerivedCategory.{w'} D]
    [EnoughInjectives C] [Abelian.HasKInjectiveResolutions C]
    (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits F]
    (I : CochainComplex C ℤ) [I.IsKInjective] (n : ℤ)
    (h : IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor D n).map
      (F.rightDerivedFunctor.map
        ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ n).app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj I))))) :
    IsIso (cokernel.desc (F.map (I.sc n).homologyData.left.f')
      (F.map (I.sc n).homologyData.left.π) (by
        rw [← F.map_comp, (I.sc n).homologyData.left.f'_π, F.map_zero]))
